general.temas: The war in Ukraine dominates several front pages, with reports on the fighting, attacks on the Crimean Bridge and prospects for negotiations. Other recurring stories include the postponement of a bill to allow remote wine sales, Estonia’s preparations to govern from abroad and the death of Mexican drug trafficker Félix Gallardo. Only Kommersant highlights the large protests in Prague over public broadcasting.
general.motivo_crispacion: Tensions are high because of the war between Russia and Ukraine, with reports of fighting, drone attacks and damage or restrictions on the Crimean Bridge. Adding to this are EU sanctions against Russia, Estonia’s announced border closure and protests in Prague over public broadcasting. The prospects for negotiations and stories about culture, sport, consumer affairs and educational cooperation offer less contentious subjects, though they do not offset the weight of the war coverage.

Kommersant.resumen:
- Yemeni government forces withdraw from coastal areas after clashes with the Houthis.
- A Moscow court sentences a former Ingush judicial official to eight years in prison in a corruption case.
- An accountant is charged over an explosion at a children’s store in Moscow.
- The front page covers the moratorium on nuclear testing and the protests in Prague over public broadcasting.
- In sports, the focus is on Magnus Carlsen’s poor result and Mirra Andreeva’s season; documentary film and planned changes to eSIMs are also covered.
Kommersant.motivo_populismo: The tone is predominantly factual, although phrases such as “dangerous accountant” and “resounding failure” add drama; there is no apparent appeal to the people against the elites.
Kommersant.sesgo: The selection gives space to conflicts, court cases and international events, alongside sports and culture. The wording uses wordplay and emphasizes some eye-catching episodes, without any clear political bias.

Rossíiskaya Gazeta.resumen:
- Ushakov sets out conditions for European participation in negotiations on Ukraine and says no agreement was reached to expand the format to include Moscow.
- The Duma postpones debate on mail-order wine sales, and the Central Bank sets the dollar at 82.51 rubles.
- Online purchases of foreign products are growing, and the government proposes expanding consumers’ ability to seek redress for defective products.
- Russia and China promote management training; a legal course for parents is also announced.
- The front page carries stories about craftspeople, bears and an explosives detection dog, as well as the sale of a bank card by a teenager.
Rossíiskaya Gazeta.motivo_populismo: The tone is predominantly factual, although phrases such as “his faithful dog” and the laudatory description of the craftspeople add an emotional element.
Rossíiskaya Gazeta.sesgo: The selection and wording give prominence to Russian official sources, especially in stories about Ukraine, and use the Russian term “special operation.” Institutional initiatives and positive local stories also feature prominently.

Komsomólskaya Pravda.resumen:
- Fighting in Ukraine and Ukrainian counterattacks ahead of negotiations in the Emirates.
- Equipment sent to the front, donations to service members and initiatives for veterans.
- A meeting between Putin and Trump on Ukraine is expected before a meeting with Xi Jinping.
- A woman suspected of an attack is detained, and Mexican drug trafficker Miguel Ángel Félix Gallardo dies.
- An Estonian plan to govern remotely, a time machine project, and culture and society news.
Komsomólskaya Pravda.motivo_populismo: Phrases such as “the home front, for victory,” “all roads are open” and “the Estonian authorities prepared to flee” combine rallying language, simplification and dramatization.
Komsomólskaya Pravda.sesgo: The front page prioritizes a perspective favorable to the Russian military effort, presenting aid to the front as a contribution to a “common victory” and highlighting positive stories about veterans. The headline about Estonia takes an alarmist approach to what is described as a plan for remote government.

Védomosti.resumen:
- Putin will attend the APEC summit; a decision on his attendance at the G20 will be made later.
- Ukrainian drone attacks affected the Crimean Bridge and several regions; people were injured in some of those regions.
- The Duma postponed the bill to allow online sales of Russian wine.
- Operators requested permission to use data centers abroad; the authorities backed a land-use planning reform.
- The front page also covers markets, exports and the Russian deputy prime minister’s visit to Kabul.
Védomosti.motivo_populismo: The headlines are mostly descriptive and avoid disparagement, appeals to the people or explicitly confrontational language.
Védomosti.sesgo: A Russian and institutional perspective predominates, with attention to the presidential agenda, the authorities and the effects of Ukrainian attacks. The selection combines these subjects with economic and regulatory news.

Meduza.resumen:
- War in Ukraine: an attack on the Crimean Bridge and new details about damage at the port of Ust-Luga.
- European countries warn of the risk of a nuclear accident and call on Russia to stop attacks on Ukrainian energy infrastructure.
- Estonia will close its border crossings with Russia; the EU expands sanctions against Russian entities and Tatiana Kim.
- The FSB reports an arrest over an attack on a former agent’s car; politician Yulia Galyamina is fined after being detained.
- Mexican drug trafficker Félix Gallardo dies, Telegram is blocked in Jordan and Iraq, and Gérard Depardieu withdraws his appeal and apologizes.
Meduza.motivo_populismo: The tone is predominantly factual, although phrases such as “growing nuclear risk” and the alleged decision to “kill Zelensky” add drama; the latter is presented as an attributed and unconfirmed claim.
Meduza.sesgo: The selection highlights the war, its consequences and measures against Russia, with attention to Russian attacks and actions by the authorities. It also includes statements from the Kremlin and other attributed accounts.

opiniones.comunista:
Today I see the same dispute behind different news stories: who controls the resources on which the majority depends? The protests in Prague in defense of public broadcasting are a reminder that information must not be left at the mercy of private profit. I stand for independent public media, adequately funded and subject to democratic oversight, not to the whims of governments or powerful financial interests.

I am also troubled by European warnings about the nuclear risk in Ukraine amid Russian attacks on energy infrastructure. The working class needs peace, electricity and public services, not a war that puts civilian lives at risk. I demand an end to attacks on that infrastructure and negotiations aimed at a lasting peace. Because energy matters to everyone, it should be collectively owned and democratically managed, not run for the profit of a few.
opiniones.anarquista:
The news about negotiations over Ukraine once again puts governments at the center of peace. I want the fighting to stop, but I distrust a peace decided solely from above: those who bear the burden of war must be able to organize and have a voice, without being subordinated to states or parties.

I am also concerned about the blocking of Telegram in Jordan and Iraq. Invoking extremism to restrict a communication tool penalizes the freedom of many people at once. Security should not be an excuse to hand the authorities control over our conversations.

In the face of the logic of command, I stand for communities able to coordinate freely, sustain themselves through mutual aid and manage their own affairs. Individual freedom needs that solidarity; collective freedom requires that no one can impose a master on it.
opiniones.liberal:
The postponement of the bill to allow online wine sales reminds me how hard it is to make room for economic freedom. I would prefer clear rules to protect consumers and prevent sales to minors, but not unnecessary obstacles that limit competition and choice. Similarly, requiring a qualified electronic signature for eSIM procedures may combat fraud, but its cost and effectiveness deserve scrutiny: security should not become an excuse to make life more complicated for everyone.

I also oppose the blocking of Telegram in Jordan and Iraq. Prosecuting specific crimes is legitimate; restricting communication for entire groups of users is a disproportionate response. I stand for limited government, low taxes and responsible citizens: freedom requires accepting consequences, but also being able to decide without asking permission at every step.
opiniones.extrema_derecha:
The attack on the Crimean Bridge and the new European sanctions remind me that sovereignty is not defended with statements. Russia needs to protect its infrastructure, retain control over its citizens’ data and negotiate from a position of security, not dependence. That is why I oppose using foreign data centers without strict safeguards. And if Estonia decides to close its border, we too must exercise our right to control who enters and under what conditions without hesitation.

But a strong nation is not just a vigilant state. Belgorod’s traditional crafts deserve support because they pass on a way of life that no elite can replace. And the corruption conviction in Ingushetia is a reminder that authority commands respect only when the law also reaches those in important positions.
opiniones.centro:
I am concerned that news about Ukraine combines possible negotiations with warnings from European countries about the risk of a nuclear catastrophe. Russia must stop attacks on Ukrainian energy infrastructure; protecting civilians cannot be subordinated to military calculations. Diplomacy is indispensable, but a lasting peace requires verifiable guarantees and the participation of those who will have to live with its consequences.

I also see an opportunity in the Russian bill that would allow consumers to bring court claims over defects discovered during the warranty period, even after it expires. A competitive market needs consumers with enforceable rights, not just companies free to sell. I would support that reform, provided it establishes clear rules and accessible procedures: institutions gain legitimacy when they solve everyday problems without sacrificing legal certainty.
